Henrike

SQL Server Upgrade Impact for Tricentis Tosca 2025

Important Note: The available SAP documentation covers SQL Server upgrades in the context of SAP NetWeaver-based systems. Tricentis Tosca is a test automation tool that integrates with SAP Solution Manager, and its specific SQL Server compatibility matrix should be verified directly with Tricentis/SAP support. The guidance below reflects SAP's documented SQL Server 2025 upgrade considerations and known edition-related issues that are relevant to your planning.

Compatibility Considerations
  • No accepted answer exists yet for the specific question of Tricentis Tosca 2025 compatibility with SQL Server 2025 — the community thread matching your exact scenario (Tosca 2025 + SQL Server 2022 Enterprise → SQL Server 2025 Standard) was posted on 10-09-2026 and currently has 0 accepted solutions and 0 answers. [1] You should raise a formal SAP support ticket to obtain a definitive compatibility statement before proceeding.
  • SAP's official documentation confirms that SQL Server 2025 upgrade is supported from SQL Server 2022 (16.x) as a valid upgrade path, and SQL Server 2022 users do not need to apply any additional SPS (Support Package Stack) before upgrading to SQL Server 2025. [2]
  • SQL Server 2025 is only available for 64-bit platforms; cross-platform upgrades are not supported. [3]
Enterprise → Standard Edition: Key Impacts
Area Enterprise Edition Standard Edition
DBCON / ABAP Connectivity (EngineEdition)EngineEdition = 3 (required by DBSL library for MSSQL_SE=1 connections)EngineEdition = 2 — DBSL library will reject the connection with error: "The DBSL library supports only connections to the SQL Server Database Engine with the Engine Edition = 3" [4]
Edition Downgrade PathEnterprise → Standard is a supported edition upgrade path in SQL Server 2025 [3] [5]Standard edition is a valid target, but feature availability must be verified before downgrading
High Availability FeaturesFull HA features (AlwaysOn AG, Failover Clustering) supportedSome HA features are limited or unavailable in Standard Edition — verify your HA topology [3]
Feature CompatibilityFull Enterprise feature setVerify that all features currently in use are supported in Standard Edition before proceeding [6]

⚠️ Critical Warning on Edition Change: SAP KBA 3739963 explicitly documents that when connecting an ABAP system to an external SQL Server 2025 Standard Developer edition (EngineEdition = 2), the DBSL library blocks the connection because it only supports EngineEdition = 3 (Enterprise). [4] While this KBA specifically references the "Standard Developer edition," the underlying EngineEdition = 2 applies to Standard edition as well. You must confirm with SAP Support whether the Standard (non-Developer) edition of SQL Server 2025 is supported for your specific Tosca/SAP integration before proceeding with the edition downgrade.

Prerequisites & Precautions
  1. Verify SAP Note 3649352: Confirm the minimum recommended SPS level for SQL Server 2025 compatibility with your SAP/Tosca landscape. Since you are on SQL Server 2022, no additional SPS is required prior to the SQL Server upgrade itself, but the minimum SPS for SQL Server 2025 must still be met. [2]
  2. Import latest SAP kernel patches and dbsl library: Ensure the latest kernel patches, dbsl library, and support package stacks are applied at or above the minimum level specified for SQL Server 2025. These are available on the SAP Support Portal under Software Downloads (see SAP Note 19466). [2]
  3. Verify feature usage vs. Standard Edition: Before downgrading from Enterprise to Standard, confirm that every SQL Server feature currently used by Tosca and any connected SAP systems is supported in Standard Edition. [3] [6]
  4. Check for pending restarts: The SQL Server 2025 upgrade will be blocked if there is a pending system restart, if the Windows Installer Service is not running, or if performance counters are corrupt. [2]
  5. Confirm 64-bit environment: SQL Server 2025 is only supported on 64-bit platforms. [3]
  6. Confirm Windows OS compatibility: SQL Server 2025 installation requires Windows Server 2019 Standard/Datacenter or Windows Server 2022 Standard/Datacenter. [7]
  7. Raise an SAP Support ticket: Given the open community question with no accepted answer [1], formally engage SAP Support (category: SOLMAN Test Suite / SAP Solution Manager) to obtain a certified compatibility statement for Tosca 2025 with SQL Server 2025 Standard Edition.
  8. Full database backup: Take a complete backup of all databases before initiating any upgrade activity. [8] [2]
Recommended Upgrade Steps
  1. Perform a full backup of all databases and verify backup integrity before starting.
  2. Shut down the SAP/Tosca application before beginning the SQL Server upgrade. [2]
  3. Apply latest SAP kernel patches and dbsl library to meet the SQL Server 2025 minimum requirements (SAP Note 3649352 and SAP Note 19466).
  4. Run the SQL Server 2025 setup and select "Upgrade from a previous version of SQL Server" — follow the prompts, specifying the correct instance. Note: You cannot use the SQL4SAP script to upgrade from SQL Server 2022 to SQL Server 2025; the SQL4SAP script does not support this upgrade path. [7]
  5. Post-SQL upgrade verification: Confirm the SQL Server version, check SQL Server error logs for any errors, and test database connectivity. [8]
  6. Perform the edition change (Enterprise → Standard) as a separate step after the version upgrade is confirmed stable, following Microsoft's "Upgrade to a different edition of SQL Server (Setup)" procedure. [3] [5]
  7. Restart the SAP/Tosca system and validate that all services are running correctly, all Tosca test connections are functional, and run a regression check. [8]
  8. Develop a rollback plan before starting — ensure you can restore the original SQL Server 2022 Enterprise environment if issues arise. [9]

entry.title: Re: Processing RFC Queues errors on EWM SAP Public Cloud
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Joule Response

Reprocessing qRFC in SAP EWM Public Cloud
Issue Summary

You have a stuck qRFC queue (DLWS0M8E6E4 0080000423) in SAP EWM Public Cloud with the error:

Command to tRFC/qRFC: Execute LUW again — Message no. /SCWM/MONITOR064

This message is classified by SAP as "self-explanatory," but in practice it does not reveal the underlying root cause directly. The real error is often hidden behind this generic status, and the queue remains in RETRY state. [1]

Resolution Steps

Step 1: Verify Queue Status via Dashboard Messages Tile

Since you found no queues in the Dashboard Messages tile, the queue may not be surfacing there due to how Public Cloud exposes qRFC errors. Instead, navigate directly to the Warehouse Monitor:

  • Go to /SCWM/MON → Tools → Message Queue
  • Locate the stuck queue (DLWS* prefix)
  • Check the error status and attempt reprocessing from there [2]

Step 2: Attempt Debug LUW in the Monitor

Per SAP KBA 3555285, the "Execute LUW again" message can sometimes appear because the application log is too large to display — not necessarily because there is a real blocking error. The recommended action is: [3]

  1. Click the Debug LUW button on the stuck queue
  2. Press F8 to execute
  3. If no error appears during execution, the queue may actually process successfully
  4. If an error does appear, set a breakpoint on function module /SCWM/TO_CREATE_WHR and check variable lt_bapiret for the actual error detail [3]

Step 3: Check SLG1 Application Log

Even if the queue monitor shows no detail, check transaction SLG1 for application logs around the timestamp of the queue failure. Filter by the queue name or the user ID associated with the stuck queue. This often reveals the true blocking error (e.g., authorization issue, lock conflict, or customizing gap). [4] [5]

Step 4: Check for Authorization Issues (SU53)

A common hidden cause for this error is a missing authorization. After the queue failure, run transaction SU53 with the user that triggered the queue. If a missing authorization object is displayed, assign it and then reprocess the queue. [6]

Step 5: Engage SAP Support

Since you are on SAP EWM Public Cloud, direct queue debugging (e.g., production debug access) is restricted. If the above steps do not resolve the issue: [7] [5]

  • Raise a support case under component SCM-EWM-DLP (Delivery Processing) or SCM-EWM-WOP (Warehouse Order Processing), depending on the queue type
  • Reference KBA 3258037 (WMDPDO/WMDPDI queues in RETRY with SR053) and KBA 3555285 (WM* queue with "Execute LUW again") in your case
  • SAP Support will debug the queue in the production environment to identify the exact root cause [8] [9]
Key Considerations

Quantity Adjustment Impact on S/4HANA Sync

  • You adjusted the quantity to 0 on the EWM side, but the S/4HANA side has not yet received this update — this is precisely because the qRFC carrying the confirmation is stuck.
  • Until the queue is successfully processed (or cleared by SAP Support), the two systems will remain out of sync.
  • Do not manually force-delete the queue without SAP Support guidance, as this can cause permanent data inconsistencies between EWM and S/4HANA. [2]

Known Limitation in EWM Public Cloud for qRFC Reprocessing

  • In the Public Cloud environment, standard on-premise tools like direct SMQ1/SMQ2 access and production debugging are not available to customers — this is a confirmed constraint, which is why the SAP Community thread you referenced advises contacting SAP Support. [7]
  • The Warehouse Monitor (/SCWM/MON → Tools → Message Queue) is the primary self-service tool available in Public Cloud for queue visibility and reprocessing attempts. [2] [10]
  • If the queue cannot be reprocessed via the monitor, SAP Support is the required escalation path for Public Cloud environments.

entry.title: Re: defective quantity on api API_QUALITYNOTIFICATION
entry.content:
You are right, there is no such field on the header. I checked on an S/4HANA 2023 system: the header entity of API_QUALITYNOTIFICATION has no quantity field at all, and the defective quantities exist only on the item.

What I measured

  • The header entity QualityNotification is the CDS view A_QltyNotification, a projection on R_QltyNotificationTP. It has type, texts, codes, dates, supplier, customer, material, plant, purchasing data, inspection lot, batch and material document, and no quantity.
  • The business object under it already knows two header quantities: its behavior maps NotificationComplaintQuantity to QMEL-RKMNG and NotificationExternalQty to QMEL-MGFRD (Defective Quantity (External)). The internal one, QMEL-MGEIG, is not even in that view. The API projection exposes none of them.
  • A_QltyNotification is released only for remote use (C2). The extension contract (C0) is not released and the projection behavior is not marked extensible, so you cannot add the standard field to the API with developer extensibility.
  • The header behavior only allows create, no update, so this API cannot change header fields of an existing notification anyway.
  • The item entity QualityNotificationItem has ExternalDefectiveQuantity (QMFE-FMGFRD) and InternalDefectiveQuantity (QMFE-FMGEIG). DefectiveQuantityUnit is read only.

I also ran it: I created a Q2 notification through the API business object (EML on A_QltyNotification, no commit, rolled back) with one item with ExternalDefectiveQuantity 3 and InternalDefectiveQuantity 1. FAILED was empty, REPORTED returned no texts, and reading the item back gave 3 and 1. The unit came back empty: it is read only, and I did not test when it gets filled.

What you can do

  • Inside this API, the item is the only place for a defective quantity.
  • On premise or private cloud, if it must be the header: QMEL-MGFRD and QMEL-MGEIG are in the header structure RIQS5 of the RFC function module IQS4_CREATE_NOTIFICATION. I called it with I_POST = space, so nothing was saved. With the default I_CHECK_PARNR_COMP = 'X' it stopped with error IX 200 for partner functions KU (Coordinator) and LF (Supplier, VN on English screens), which are mandatory for Q2 in my system. With I_CHECK_PARNR_COMP = space the header came back with a temporary number, RKMNG 10, MGFRD 5 and MGEIG 2. In a real call, pass the partners in I_IHPA_T instead of switching the check off.
  • This function module is not a released API, so it is for classic ABAP or RFC only. BAPI_QUALNOT_CREATE does not help here: its header (BAPI2078_NOTHDRI) has QUANT_COMPLAINT for the complaint quantity, and no defective quantity.
  • The field documentation says external plus internal must not exceed the complaint quantity. In my run the function module did not check that before save: 8 and 5 against a complaint quantity of 10 came back with no error. If you go this way, check it on your side.
  • If you are on the public cloud, open the $metadata of your service and look at the QualityNotification entity: if it has no quantity property, it is the same situation, and the item is the way.

What I did not test: saving the notification in either path, passing the partners in I_IHPA_T, calling the OData service over HTTP, the maintenance notification API you mentioned, and releases after 2023 or the public cloud. The API fields, the mapping and the runs above are measured.

entry.title: From V1 to V2: Transitioning to SAP Sales Cloud & SAP Service Cloud V2 with Confidence
entry.content:
From V1 to V2: Transitioning to SAP Sales Cloud & SAP Service Cloud V2 with Confidence

Moving from SAP Sales Cloud & SAP Service Cloud V1 to V2 is not a routine upgrade. For customers who have spent years building deeply customized processes, it requires careful planning and the right tooling. This article explains what the transition really involves, the questions every customer is asking, and how a set of purpose-built tools makes the journey structured, predictable, and significantly less costly— and addresses the real-world concerns practitioners are raising in the community.

UNDERSTANDING THE SHIFT
This Is Not an Upgrade — It Is a Re-Platforming (And That Is a Good Thing)

The distinction matters. The transition to SAP Sales Cloud & Service Cloud V2 is more than a technology change—it is an opportunity to rethink and modernize how the business operates.

Many customers have built significant business capabilities on SAP Sales Cloud & Service Cloud through PDI-based extensions written in ABSL. As V2 introduces a cloud-native, microservices-based architecture on SAP BTP and follows the Clean Core principle, these customizations do not have a direct lift-and-shift path. Customizations, integrations, and custom business objects therefore need to be assessed and thoughtfully transitioned to the new architecture.

This creates a unique opportunity for customers to step back and ask: What should we carry forward, what can we simplify, and what can we do better? Rather than simply recreating the existing solution, customers can use the transition to:

  • Harmonize business processes and eliminate unnecessary complexity
  • Adopt standard capabilities where V2 has closed the gap
  • Identify where AI and automation can deliver greater efficiency and a better user experience
  • Establish a scalable, maintainable Clean Core foundation for the future

The transition is therefore not just a technical exercise or a rebuild of existing functionality. It is a business transformation opportunity—enabling customers to modernize their processes, preserve what differentiates their business, embrace intelligent capabilities, and build on an architecture designed for the next decade of innovation.

STRUCTURAL CHALLENGES
Three Forces Driving Customer Uncertainty
Customer hesitation around the V1-to-V2 transition is not unwillingness to modernize. It comes from three structural realities that, left unaddressed, make the journey feel complex and costly.

1. Deeply Customized Processes

The vast majority of V1 customers have built custom extensions and business logic that are central to how they operate. These cannot be migrated wholesale — they must be re-engineered, with care taken to preserve competitive differentiation.

2. A Complete Re-Platforming

Moving from monolithic V1 with PDI extensions to V2’s microservices architecture on BTP is not a version bump. Development teams must move from ABSL to CAP Node.js and adopt a fundamentally different extension model.

3. High Cost Without Structure

Without a defined methodology, every project starts from scratch. Cost overruns, timeline uncertainty, and the absence of repeatable patterns stall investment decisions and erode confidence.

THE VOICE OF THE CUSTOMER
The Questions Every Customer Is Asking

Customer conversations at the start of this transition journey consistently surface the same concerns. These are not objections to be managed — they are legitimate questions that deserve concrete answers.

  • Are we looking at a platform change or just a version update?
  • Will our current setup carry over, or does everything need to be rebuilt from scratch?
  • Does moving to V2 mean we lose everything we built in V1?
  • All our custom code and tailored fields — what happens to them?
  • How do we realistically size this in terms of time and budget?
  • Is there a proven path others have followed, or are we on our own?
  • Could this transition be the right moment to bring AI into our day-to-day processes?

TRANSITION ANATOMY
Where the Effort Actually Goes

Understanding how transition effort is distributed helps customers plan resources and set realistic expectations early. The four workstreams below account for the full transition scope.

Workstream

Effort Share

Description

Custom Extensions

40–50%

PDI/ABSL script & CBO transformation to BTP CAP — the single largest effort area

Business Processes

20–30%

Standard feature adoption, UI personalization, configuration and process setup

Integration

~15-20%

Standard and custom integrations

Data Migration

~15-20%

Historical data transfer, validation, and bulk data processing


THE TOOLING ECOSYSTEM
A Purpose-Built Toolkit for Every Phase

SAP has developed a suite of transition tools covering the entire transition lifecycle — from first assessment to go-live. Each tool targets a specific challenge that has historically caused delays or cost overruns. Together, they turn a high-risk, bespoke exercise into a structured, repeatable, and measurably faster process.

1. Pre-Assessment - Parity Check Questionnaire
Structured feature-by-feature comparison of V1 capabilities against V2. Identifies gaps and guides transition scope definition.

The Parity Check Questionnaire provides a structured, feature-by-feature comparison of SAP Sales and Service Cloud V1 capabilities against V2. It helps identify feature gaps, assess feature compatibility, and define the migration scope. By evaluating your current feature usage, the questionnaire helps determine how ready your V1 system is for transition to V2 and highlights areas that may require further assessment or planning.

What you get:

  • Identify the features activated in your current V1 system.
  • Determine whether the features you use in V1 are available in V2.
  • For features not currently available in V2, understand whether they are planned for the product roadmap, helping inform migration decisions and next steps. 

How you get it: available as part of a guided transition engagement. Reach out to your SAP Contact or SAP Professional Services team to get more information.

2. Readiness Check Tool 
Knowing what features exist in V2 is one thing. Knowing whether your organization is actually ready to begin the transition — and what blockers exist — is another.

The Readiness Check Tool evaluates your current V1 landscape — customizations, integrations, data, and processes —Think of it as a health check before you begin.

What you get:

  • See exactly what is in your V1 system — extension fields, PDIs, mashups, and configuration scope
  • Know what moves to V2 automatically, what needs manual work, and what is not supported
  • Functional readiness for V2 transition
  • Walk into planning with a report, not assumptions

How you get it: Available out of the box as standard feature
Readiness Check Tool | SAP Help Portal

3. AssessMate — AI-Powered Extension & Integration Analysis
Manually reviewing hundreds of V1 PDI extensions & integrations to understand complexity, transition effort, and V2 mapping can take weeks and is prone to inconsistency. AssessMate does it in a fraction of the time.

 AssessMate reads it, analyses every custom object and script, and produces a structured report summarizing what you have, how complex it is to move, and what the effort looks like. entry.content:

Thank you very much for your question.

Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Joule Response

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Legacy to Subscription User License Mapping

This is an excellent and highly practical question for sizing and licensing estimation. Based on official SAP documentation and the nested licensing model described for SAP Cloud ERP, here is the most accurate mapping guidance available.

Legacy vs. Subscription User Type Mapping Matrix
Legacy User Type Subscription Equivalent(s) Notes
Self-ServiceSelf-Service (SAP Finance & SCM Self-Service)Direct 1:1 mapping. Covers occasional tasks like time entry, workflow approvals, paystub access.
CoreOperational (primary) + Finance Base + SCM Base (as applicable)Core maps to the "middle tier" of the nested model. Operational is the closest direct equivalent; Finance Base and SCM Base are elevated Core-tier licenses with additional entitlements.
AdvancedFinance Premium + SCM Premium + Finance Base & SCM Base comboAdvanced maps to the highest-capability tiers. Finance Base and SCM Base are NOT Advanced — they sit at the Core tier level.
Key Mapping Clarifications

Core → Subscription Mapping

The legacy Core user type maps to what SAP now calls the "middle tier" of the nested subscription model. Specifically: [1]

  • Operational is the closest direct equivalent to a Core user — covering users engaged in core processes such as sales, inventory, or procurement.
  • Finance Base and SCM Base are also within the Core tier family, but they are elevated versions that include additional entitlements (e.g., SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity, SAP Market Rates Management, SAP Integrated Development) beyond what a plain Operational user receives. [1]
  • The nested model confirms: "a Finance Base User can access everything that an operational user can do and more" — meaning Finance Base ⊃ Operational ⊃ Self-Service. [1]

Practical guidance: A user classified as Core in your TDD environment should be mapped to Operational unless their role specifically requires Finance or SCM Base entitlements. Finance Base and SCM Base are Core-tier licenses, not Advanced.

Advanced → Subscription Mapping

The legacy Advanced user type maps to the Premium tiers in the new subscription model: [1]

  • Finance Premium — includes all Finance Base capabilities plus advanced entitlements (SAP Concur, SAP Ariba, SAP Sales Cloud V2, SAP Project & Resource Management, etc.) [1]
  • SCM Premium — includes all SCM Base capabilities plus advanced sustainability and compliance entitlements (SAP Sustainability Footprint Management, EHS solutions, etc.) [1]
  • Finance Base & SCM Base combo — this combination license is designed for super users needing broad authorization across both Finance and SCM scope areas, and sits at the upper boundary of the Core tier / lower boundary of Advanced. [1]

Critical clarification: Finance Base and SCM Base are NOT Advanced — they are Core-tier licenses. Only Finance Premium and SCM Premium (and the combo) represent the Advanced tier. [1]

The FUE weighting model (used in the legacy RISE model) confirms this hierarchy: 1 FUE = 1 Advanced user, but 1 FUE = 5 Core users — reflecting the significant capability and cost difference. [2] [3]

Sizing & Estimation Guidance

  • Avoid overclassification: Since your TDD environment reports roles as either "Core" or "Advanced," the key risk is mapping all Finance Base / SCM Base users as Advanced. These are Core-tier licenses. Only users requiring Premium-tier entitlements (Concur, Ariba, Sales Cloud V2, EHS, Sustainability tools, etc.) should be classified as Advanced/Premium. [1]

  • Use the IAM Information System app: To proactively identify which business roles and business catalogs map to which price category (Self-Service / Core / Advanced), use the IAM Information System app in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Navigate to the Business Role – Business Catalog tab to correlate roles with their pricing category — including at the individual catalog level, not just the role level. [4]

  • Validate via Maintain Business User app: Once roles are assigned, the Maintain Business User app will display the resulting license classification for each user. This allows you to verify the impact before go-live. [5]

  • SAP for Me – License Consumption: You can track licensed FUE/User Subscription quantities and consumption via SAP for Me: Reporting → License Consumption under metric CY334. [6]

  • Official reference: The legally binding user type definitions are in the SAP Cloud ERP Service Use Description, available at the SAP Trust Center. This document provides the authoritative mapping of capabilities per user type. [7]

Summary Mapping at a Glance
 
Self-Service  →  Self-Service (unchanged)
Core          →  Operational (direct match)
                 Finance Base (Core-tier, with Finance entitlements)
                 SCM Base (Core-tier, with SCM entitlements)
Advanced      →  Finance Premium (Advanced-tier)
                 SCM Premium (Advanced-tier)
                 Finance Base & SCM Base Combo (super-user, upper Core/Advanced boundary)

The nested model is the key principle: each higher tier includes all capabilities of the tier below it. Finance Base ⊃ Operational ⊃ Self-Service; Finance Premium ⊃ Finance Base. [1]

  • [1] Describing SAP Cloud ERP LicensingSAP Learning
  • [4] How to identify which Business Catalogs to which user type license (advanced / core / self-service)SAP Community
  • [5] Users LicenseSAP Community
  • [6] GROW with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, baseSAP Community
  • [7] Understanding Subscription LicensingSAP Learning

entry.title: Re: Exclude Custom Fields from ORDER_CONFIRMATION_CHANGE
entry.content:
The row with the blank Field Name is a catch all for the whole item line, and that table has no exclude option. In customizing you can only replace it with a list of the fields that must count. I checked and ran it on an S/4HANA 2023 system.

What I measured

  • The rows are in table OMCHGDOC_FIELD, maintained with view OMCD_V1_FIELDV (IMG activity "Assign Output Texts to Document Data"). The key is application object type, output type, table and field name. Besides the key there are only the text ID and the group text ID, no exclude flag. The only table in this area with an exclusion indicator, OMCHGDOC_FILTER, works per receiver, role and channel, and its short text says obsolete.
  • Delivered rows for ORDER_CONFIRMATION_CHANGE in my system: VBAP with blank field, ABGRU, KWMENG, MATNR, NETPR and NETWR; VBAK VDATU; VBEP with blank field, BMENG and EDATU.
  • The check is CL_OM_CHGDOC_UTIL=>CHECK_CHG_TABLE, called from CL_OM_CHGDOC in method IF_CDO_OR_ITEM_VALIDATOR~VALIDATE_OR_ITEM. A row with a field name compares only that field, and only for updated lines. The row with the blank field name does more than follow the update indicator: it reports every inserted or deleted item, and for an updated item it moves the old and the new line into a structure of type VBAP and compares the whole line. Fields from an append on VBAP are components of VBAP, so a change in any custom field counts. There is no BAdI or exit in this check, nor in the classes around it (CL_OM_CHGDOC and CL_OM_CHGDOC_SALES).

I also ran it: I called that method with the delivered rows and an old and a new item line in memory. No sales order was changed and nothing was saved. My system has no custom fields on VBAP, so I changed ARKTX, a standard field that is not in the list and goes through the same code.

  • Only ARKTX changed, delivered rows: changed, reported by the blank VBAP row with update indicator U (text "The item was updated."), and the log of the check names VBAP-ARKTX as the difference.
  • Only ARKTX changed, without the blank VBAP row: not changed.
  • Only KWMENG changed, without the blank VBAP row: changed, through the KWMENG row (text "The item quantity changed.").
  • New item, only the item line: not changed without the blank VBAP row, changed with it (update indicator I, "The item was added.").
  • New item with its schedule line, without the blank VBAP row: changed, through the blank VBEP row ("The schedule line was added.").

What you can do

  • For ORDER_CONFIRMATION_CHANGE, remove the VBAP row with the blank field name and add one row for each VBAP field that must trigger the change output. Your custom fields simply stay out of that list.
  • Side effect: a new or deleted item is then reported through its schedule lines (blank VBEP row), with the schedule line text instead of the item text. An item without schedule lines would not be reported by these table rows on insert or delete.
  • About the delete: in my system the view does not block it. The table has delivery class C, the view has no maintenance restriction, and its only event is a check for new entries. I did not try the delete itself, so if your system refuses it, please post the exact error text.
  • Keeping the catch all and leaving out only some fields would need a change in CL_OM_CHGDOC_UTIL, which is not released. I did not test that.

What I did not test: a real change in VA02 with output determination and the form, the delete and new rows in the view (I did not run its check for new entries), items without schedule lines, and releases after 2023 or the public cloud. The table contents, the code path and the runs above are measured.

Hello @R_Pooja 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, company-code restrictions are available through standard business-role authorizations, but restricting automatic payment runs to a predefined list of individual suppliers is not supported by the standard supplier authorization-group restriction.

1. Restrict payments by company code

Use the Maintain Business Roles app and review the restrictions for the business catalog SAP_FIN_BC_APAR_PAY_PC, which controls the Manage Automatic Payments (F0770) app.

You can restrict access by company code and control which payment-processing activities users can perform, such as scheduling payment parameters, proposals and payments.

Reference: SAP KBA 3727647 – Restricting scheduling functions in Manage Automatic Payments
https://userapps.support.sap.com/sap/support/knowledge/en/3727647


2. Restrict payments by individual supplier

SAP confirms that the restriction type Authorization Group for Supplier works for value help but does not control authorization for payment proposals and payment runs.

Reference: SAP KBA 3631758 – Authorization Group for Supplier only works for value help
https://userapps.support.sap.com/sap/support/knowledge/en/3631758

Therefore, do not rely on supplier authorization groups or payment-run selection parameters as a security control for restricting payments to specific suppliers.

entry.title: onedevatlas is open: one connected graph for SAP developers

Today onedevatlas opens to everyone. It is one connected graph of what is built for SAP development, by SAP and by everyone else: packages, plugins, services, tools, MCP servers and skills, the problems they answer, the posts and talks that explain them, and the people who make them. One graph, read by people and by their agents.

Why it exists

Building has never been easier, and being found has never been harder. On 3 October the atlas listed 31 MCP servers for ABAP. Today it lists 42. Most of them are careful work, and many solve the same problem, because their makers could not see what was already there. Agents make it sharper: an agent knows what it was trained on and what the skills beside it describe, and the work of a freelancer, a partner or a customer team is rarely part of its answer.

The lists we have, for CAP, for UI5, for ABAP, are good and separate. What was missing is a view across the stacks, with SAP's work and the community's side by side, and a graph underneath that says how things relate.

 

A map drawn by capability

Every door, CAP, UI5, ABAP and BTP, and the smaller ones for SAP Commerce, SAP SuccessFactors and SAP Digital Manufacturing, has its own map. One hexagon is one capability, a concern a project has, and its colour says who is present: SAP, the community, both, or nobody yet. Open a tile and the capability page says what SAP ships, where that stops, and who else is present. Under a capability, use cases make the options comparable by the outcome they cover and the conditions under which they cover it, never by stars or downloads.

Behind the map is the graph itself, at /graph: select a node and its card says what it provides, who maintains it and what it depends on, each edge with one meaning.

The same answers for your agent

The hosted MCP server at https://onedevatlas.dev/mcp answers with the same facts the pages show. This exchange was recorded against the live server today: a question about letting a coding agent change ABAP in an on-premise system lands on a capability, then on an assessed use case with seven options, six covering it under conditions and one not known, and the four things that decide between them for your system.

Explore, and TechEd week

The third way in is a flight. Explore and Play is the same graph as a place: make an orb, design a ship and fly through the ecosystems. Until Sunday 1 November, midnight in Berlin, it is shared: sign in with GitHub, meet other pilots, play rock, paper, scissors (SAP style) and collect points for what you look at. Then the boards freeze, and the leaders stay in the atlas's history.

 

Take part

If your work is missing or something about it is wrong, open an issue. Anything about a person goes directly through the contact form. Maintainers can sign in and write a note on their own entry.

The full article explains the words the atlas uses and how to read a capability page, and its discussion is open.

entry.title: Re: Inflated G/L account balances resulting from clearing...
entry.content:
Hello @xuqi_fangaf39f1 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, this is generally standard accounting behavior.

The Debit and Credit Transaction Figures in the Display G/L Account Balances app represent the total debit and credit turnover for the selected period, not just the closing balance.

When a clearing document contains new G/L postings, those debit and credit amounts are added to the transaction figures. For example:

Original posting 1,000 Dr  1,000 Cr
Clearing document 1,000 Dr 1,000 Cr
Total transaction figures 2,000 Dr 2,000 Cr

Although the debit and credit transaction figures increase, the net balance remains unchanged. This is expected when the clearing document contains offsetting postings.

Can this be prevented?

There is no standard setting to exclude posted clearing-document line items from G/L transaction figures. The accounting records must reflect the postings that have occurred.

entry.title: SAP EarlyWatch Alert: A Unified View of Missing Side-Effect Solving Notes
entry.content:
Introduction

Maintaining the stability and reliability of SAP systems involves more than implementing SAP Notes to resolve known issues. In some cases, an implemented SAP Note may introduce a known side effect that requires a corresponding side-effect solving SAP Note.

Identifying missing side-effect solving SAP Notes is essential for assessing potential risks and determining appropriate corrective actions. The SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service helps customers address this challenge by detecting missing solving notes and triggering alerts for affected systems. However, locating and reviewing this information can be challenging when the findings are spread across multiple system components and different sections of the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Report.

To make this process easier, a new functionality is available in the SAP EarlyWatch Alert experience for on-premise and private cloud systems.

What's New?

Get the complete picture at a glance! A new card in the Support tab of the System Details page in SAP for Me now provides a consolidated list of missing side-effect solving SAP Notes identified by the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service across your system's components—making it easier to spot potential issues, gain insights, and take action.

No more piecing together information from different sources! Previously, these details were scattered across individual components in the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Solution Finder results and various sections of the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Report.

With this enhancement, users can access the relevant information in one place instead of navigating through multiple components and report sections to build a complete picture.

Where Can You Find the New Overview?

The functionality is available for on-premise and private cloud systems.

To access the overview:

  1. Open the relevant system's System Details page under Systems and Provisioning in SAP for Me.
  2. Navigate to the Support tab.
  3. Locate the new card for missing side-effect solving notes.
  4. Review the consolidated findings across the system's components.

This provides a convenient starting point for understanding which missing notes have been identified and may require attention.

Which Components Are Covered?

The functionality covers the components evaluated by the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service for missing side-effect solving SAP Notes. The applicable component coverage and exclusions depend on the supported checks and system type.

For a detailed list of the components included in the checks, as well as those excluded from the overview, refer to SAP Note 3362629 – Missing Side Effects Solving SAP Notes Detected by SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service.

 

How Can You Use This Information?

The consolidated overview helps you identify missing side-effect solving SAP Notes and prioritize further investigation.

When reviewing the findings, consider the following steps:

  1. Review the missing notes listed for your system.
  2. Examine the corresponding SAP Notes and their relevance to the affected components.
  3. Assess the potential impact on your system and business processes.
  4. Determine the appropriate corrective actions based on the applicable SAP Note instructions and your system's requirements.

The overview supports your analysis and decision-making. The relevance of each finding should be assessed in the context of your individual system before implementing any changes.

“Spot missing  SAP Notes. Stay ahead of side effects.”!

entry.title: SAPAutoLogon: Connect KeePass with SAP Logon and SAP GUI
entry.content:
Introduction

Anyone who works with many SAP systems keeps logon details somewhere: system ID, application server, instance number, client, user and password. A password manager is the right place for the credentials, but the connection data is usually typed again by hand, or the session is started through SAP Logon in a separate step.

SAPAutoLogon brings both together. It is a free, open source plugin for KeePass 2.x that reads your SAP Logon configuration, fills the connection fields of a KeePass entry, and starts SAP GUI or SAP Business Client directly from the KeePass entry list.

  Importing a SAP Logon folder into a KeePass group.

What the plugin does

SAP tab in the entry dialog. The Add Entry and Edit Entry dialogs get an additional SAP tab. In Manual mode, which is the default, you enter the connection fields yourself and a status line tells you whether the entry is ready to launch.

 The SAP tab in Manual mode.

In Automatic mode a searchable list shows the systems from SAP Logon. Selecting one fills the fields, and every field stays editable. Direct application servers, logon groups with a message server, SAProuter strings and SNC are supported. If SAP Logon stores no client or language, the plugin fills client 100 and language EN.

  The SAP tab in Automatic mode, with the search box and the selected system.

The values are stored as normal string fields of the entry (systemId, applicationServer, systemNumber, messageServer, messageServerPort, group, sapRouterString, sncName, sncType, client, language and transaction). They are visible on the Advanced tab, and the database stays readable without the plugin.

Import from SAP Logon. The context menu of a KeePass group has the command Import from SAP Logon.

  The group context menu with the Import from SAP Logon command.

A window shows the SAP Logon folder tree with the number of systems per folder, a search box and a preview of what will be created. Subfolders become nested groups and systems become entries. Existing groups are reused, and entries that are already present are skipped and never changed. You can optionally set a default user name for systems that have none in SAP Logon. Imported entries receive the SAP logo as their icon.

  The Import from SAP Logon window.

Launching. The columns SAP GUI and Business Client in the entry list start the session with a double click. The same actions are in the entry context menu and on the shortcuts Ctrl+Shift+G for SAP GUI and Ctrl+Shift+N for SAP Business Client. SAP GUI is started through sapshcut.exe, whose parameters are described in SAP Note 103019, and SAP Business Client through NWBC.exe.

  Imported groups and entries with the launch columns.

Installation

  1. Download SAPAutoLogon.dll from the latest release on GitHub.
  2. Copy it into the Plugins folder of your KeePass installation.
  3. Restart KeePass.
  4. The SAP GUI and Business Client columns appear in the entry list automatically.

Requirements are Windows, KeePass 2.x, SAP GUI for Windows with sapshcut.exe and/or SAP Business Client, and SAP Logon for the system list. Without SAP Logon the SAP tab still works in Manual mode. If you used another SAP launch plugin before, remove it first. The plugin supports the KeePass update check under Help, Check for Updates.

Security considerations

Please read this section before you use the plugin with productive systems.

  • The plugin only reads the SAP Logon landscape files, including the shared landscape file, and never changes them or the registry. If the shared landscape is configured as a URL, it is fetched with a plain GET request. There is no other network access and no telemetry.
  • To log on automatically, the user name and the password of the KeePass entry are passed to sapshcut.exe as arguments. The password is therefore visible on the command line of the process while SAP GUI starts. This is how sapshcut.exe works, so decide for each system whether this is acceptable.
  • The optional default user name of the import is stored in plain text in KeePass.config.xml. Never enter a password there.
  • An import changes the database in memory. KeePass has no undo, so review the result before you save.

Source, download and feedback

  • Project page with screenshots: https://abgunes.github.io/SAPAutoLogon/
  • Source code and download (AGPL 3.0): https://github.com/abgunes/SAPAutoLogon

The plugin builds on the KPSAPLunch plugin by David Suchopar. I would be glad to hear which connection types and SAP Logon setups you use, so please leave a comment or open an issue on GitHub.

#SAP GUI, #SAPLogon, #SAPBusinessClient, #KeePass, #Security

entry.title: Re: CNIF_STATUS001 BAPI_BUS2054_SET_STATUS Resetting status &1 for object &2 not supported
entry.content:
The system status CRTD cannot be removed.

BAPI_BUS2054_SET_STATUS calls the subroutine CNIF_SYSTEM_STATUS_2054_CHECK to do the check of allowed system statuses, CRTD is not one of them:

FORM cnif_system_status_2054_check
                 USING    p_status   TYPE bapi_system_status_text
                          p_mode     TYPE bapi_status_action
                 CHANGING p_allowed  TYPE boole_d.

  p_allowed = false.

  CASE p_status.
    WHEN 'REL' OR 'REL '.
      IF p_mode = 'S'.
        p_allowed = true.
      ENDIF.
    WHEN 'LKD' OR 'LKD '.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'TECO'.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'CLSD'.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'AALK'.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'MDLK'.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'DLFL'.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'DDLK'.              "++3230129
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'PLLK'.
      p_allowed = true.
    WHEN 'BMLK'.
      p_allowed = true.      "--3230129
    WHEN space.              " no value  provided
      p_allowed = true.
  ENDCASE..

ENDFORM.

Code of BAPI_BUS2054_SET_STATUS:

  loop at I_WBS_SYSTEM_STATUS.
    if not i_wbs_system_status-undo_system_status is initial.
      PERFORM cnif_system_status_2054_check
                  USING I_WBS_SYSTEM_STATUS-undo_system_status
                        c_U
                  CHANGING
                        l_check_ok.
      IF l_check_ok = false.
        CALL FUNCTION 'METHOD_START_LOG'
          EXPORTING
            METHOD     = c_check
            OBJ_TYP    = CO1_TYPE-wbs_element
            OBJ_ID_EXT = I_WBS_SYSTEM_STATUS-wbs_element
          IMPORTING
            LOG_LEVEL  = LOG_LEVEL.
        message E001(CNIF_STATUS)
                WITH I_WBS_SYSTEM_STATUS-UNDO_SYSTEM_STATUS
                     I_WBS_SYSTEM_STATUS-WBS_ELEMENT
                     INTO NULL.

Don't try to undo the system status CRTD.

Sandra

PS: code is S/4HANA 2023 FPS 01

entry.title: 2 Key Important updates in Position Management in H2 2026
entry.content:
1. Default for Moving Currently Assigned Position Under New Manager's Position

Before this release, if you changed an employee’s manager in job information the option to "Move Currently Assigned Position Below New Manager's Position" was displayed and defaulted to No.  In the H2 2026 release there is a new setting in the Position Management Settings which enables you to default this option to Yes. This is located in the UI Customizing tab:

NOTE: the option to "Move Currently Assigned Position Below New Manager's Position" is controlled through RBP – Manage Positions – Option to Move Position to New Manager in Job Info Change.  This feature only works if you have enabled the latest editing and history UI in Configure Latest People Profile – General Settings:

Below is a reminder about how this feature behaves.  If you update an employee’s manager in Job Information it will move the employee's position (and all lower level positions) to be under the new manager's position. In this example, Chloe sits under Arjita, both as an employee and a position.

If we process the change in manager in Job Information whether through ‘take action’ or via ‘Quick Actions’, the option "Move Currently Assigned Position Below New Manager's Position" will render and will be defaulted to Yes.

When this is marked as Yes then the following will occur:

  • Chloe is moved under William
  • Chloe’s position is moved under William’s position
  • Any positions under Chloe are moved with her position
  • A job information record is added based on the event reason derivation
 
 

 

 

 

  • Position Org Chart is updated

 

 
 

 

It is important to note, that if you delete the Job Information record this will not re-adjust the positions in the org chart.  You would need to go Manage Position and delete the time slice from the position as a separate action.

2. Triggering Reclassification When Moving Positions With a Manager Change

Before this release, if you made a change in Job Information through Manager Self-Service or an Employee Central Quick Action and changed the employee's manager and another position attribute field at the same time, the Position Reclassification was simply suppressed, potentially resulting in inconsistent data between Position and Job Information. For example if you updated manager and cost center, cost center would not be updated back to the position.  You would have to process the change as two separate transactions, or make the changes on the Position object only.

In H2 2026 release there is a new setting that allows you to make the updates in one transaction

 

In the example below Chloe new Manager is Will, and her cost center is changing at the same time.

The Position Org Chart relationship is updated:

And Chloe's position is updated to reflect the new cost center:

NOTE: In order for the reclassification to work, the Job Info to Position syncing rule must be configured and on the event reason the "Follow-Up Activity in Position" option must be set to "Position Reclassification.

What key benefits does this enhancement bring?

Previously, when an employee's manager changed without the employee moving into a new position, this update was best done by HR so they could ensure both position and job information updates remained in sync with each other. The process involved either managing all changes on the position object and let the changes sync to Job Information or make the changes in a two step process in Job Information. This put more work onto HR and there was a risk to data integrity if a step was missed.  

This latest enhancement provides an intuitive and consistent way for managers to process this kind of change for their direct reports, either through MSS-Take Action or through an Employee Central Quick Action.  The data is updated in a single step, thereby reducing the risk of data errors.

More information can be found on help.sap.com here:

Moving Positions When Changing the Manager | SAP Help Portal

 Triggering Reclassification When Moving Positions With a Manager Change | SAP Help Portal

entry.title: Re: In-Process Inspection: Usage Decision Completed Witho...
entry.content:
Yes, the UD can be reversed, and with OPK4 set to error that is the way out. With the usage decision in place, the status of the lot blocks results recording, so the confirmation stays blocked by the OPK4 check. The steps are: revoke the UD, record the results, make the UD again, then confirm. I measured the status rules and ran the reset in check mode on an S/4HANA 2023 system.

What I measured

  • OPK4 is field QRMDE in table TCORU (blank, 1 for an error when no inspection results exist, 0 for nothing). Its field documentation says it controls the system reaction at order confirmation when results must be recorded for an operation and none are available yet. It talks about results only, not about the usage decision, which matches what you see.
  • The revoke is business transaction QM68 "Revoke usage decision". In the status control (table TJ07) it is allowed by status UD and prohibited by REL, CRTD, LKD, ARBL, ARCH, ILOR and LSPL. When it runs (table TJ06) it sets REL again, sets UDRE "Usage decision reset" and removes UD, ICCO, STIC, CLAS and CLQM.
  • "Record inspection results" (QM18) is allowed by REL and prohibited by UD, ICCO and STIC, among others. That is why you cannot add results after the UD, and why the revoke opens it again.
  • The code is function module QEVC_RESET_UD. It checks authorization object Q_INSPLOT with activity 18 "Reset Usage Decision", runs QM68 through status management, clears the UD flag of the lot and the UD fields (code group, code, valuation, quality score, follow up action). The Reset UD action of the inspection lot business object I_InspectionLotTP (class CL_I_A_INSPLOT_RESET_UD) calls it.
  • Field RESET_UD_ALLOWED of table TQSS1_AVE "Inspection Type-Specific Settings for Plant" (key plant and inspection type, customizing activity "Maintain settings at plant level", view cluster VC_TQSS1): its documentation says that per plant and inspection type you can allow the reset of a UD in the Manage Usage Decisions app, that the UD code, quality score and follow up action are initialized, and that stock postings are not revoked. In my system it is not set for any entry.

What I ran (check mode only, rolled back, nothing saved)

  • Lot with UD: record results refused with BS 013 "System status STIC is active"; revoke allowed; QEVC_RESET_UD in check mode passed and returned the lot without the UD flag and without the UD code.
  • Lot without UD: record results allowed; revoke refused with BS 013 "System status REL is active", and QEVC_RESET_UD raised the same error.

For your order: allow the reset for your plant and inspection type 03, give the user activity 18, revoke the UD in Manage Usage Decisions, record the results for the operation, make the UD again and confirm.

To stop the UD before results: set the characteristics of the operation as required characteristics in the routing. My system has QV 067 "Inspection lot &1: UD not possible as open required characteristics exist" and QV 062 "There are still required characteristics open for inspection lot &1". Q_INSPLOT also has activity 11 "Inspection Completion with Open Char./Insp. Pts Req. Conf", and QV 135 says "You are not authorized to close inspections with open required characs.". So the first things I would check in your setup are whether the characteristics are optional and whether the users who make the UD have activity 11.

What I did not test: an in-process lot (my system has no lots of origin 03, my test lots are origin 01, and no OPK4 entry with QRMDE set), the confirmation itself, the app screen, a real revoke with save, and a UD with open required characteristics. The tables, texts, code and the check runs above are measured.

entry.title: Authorization Control in Manage Maintenance Notifications via App Authorization Variants (AAVs)
entry.content:
Manage Maintenance Notifications (F5777) is the next-generation app for the maintenance notification lifecycle consolidating what previously required multiple apps — from creating a maintenance notification to screening, editing, accepting, and creating a maintenance order.

The same app is expected to be used by people with different responsibilities during maintenance execution, but not everyone using F5777 should be able to do the same things within it. This is exactly where authorization control can be achieved by App Authorization Variants (AAVs).

This blog focuses on the different App Authorization Variants for Manage Maintenance Notifications (F5777) app and how they can be leveraged for different roles. To know the fundamentals of App Authorization Variants, please refer to these blogs- SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2502: Flexible Business Role Design with App Authorization Variants and Precise Control of Fiori App Access with the App Authorization Variants.

The 4 AAVs of Manage Maintenance Notifications (F5777)-

Each App Authorization Variant corresponds to a persona and defines what that persona can do inside the app.

AAV

Persona

Key Capability

F5777_EMP_TRAN

Maintenance Employee or Maintenance Technician

Create maintenance notification; edit only on request.

F5777_MPL_TRAN

Maintenance Planner

Employee access along with Assign/Create maintenance orders for notifications.

F5777_TRAN

Maintenance Supervisor

Full notification lifecycle except for Order creation/assignment — create, screen, accept, edit throughout.

F5777_EXCP_TRAN

Operator

Employee access along with creation of Emergency work and Minor work.

Let us look at each one.

1. F5777_EMP_TRAN | Maintenance Employee | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_EMP_PC

This variant is designed for maintenance employees or maintenance technicians who spot issues and raise them in the system.

A user with this AAV can create maintenance notifications and read all notification types. However, their ability to edit is limited. They can only edit a notification when:

  • The notification is moved to an "Action Required" subphase,
    AND
  • Creator or the User is the or the designated Person Responsible for that notification.

This AAV is part of the standard role template SAP_BR_EMPLOYEE_MAINTENANCE, belonging to business catalog SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_EMP_PC.

Using the standard role template SAP_BR_EMPLOYEE_MAINTENANCE may enable 'Set Deletion flag' for the user due to additional business authorization coming from other catalogs in the role template.


Fig 1: Actions enabled for employee when notification is in Action Required subphase

2. F5777_MPL_TRAN | Maintenance Planner | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_MPL_PC

This AAV enables the maintenance planner to create notifications and allows to create or assign maintenance orders for accepted notifications. The Edit authorization is same as in F5777_EMP_TRAN AAV. This variant even allows user to delete and complete the notification.


Fig 2: List report view for user with AAV F5777_MPL_TRAN


Fig 3: Object page view when notification is created


Fig 4: Create and Assign Order enabled for accepted maintenance notification

The variant F5777_MPL_TRAN is part of standard role template SAP_BR_MAINTENANCE_PLANNER, belonging to business catalog SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_MPL_PC.
This role template gives additional authorizations to the user as compared to the App Authorization Variant F5777_MPL_TRAN such as- Creation of minor/emergency work, accepting, and editing the maintenance notification.


Fig 5: Additional actions enabled in standard planner role template for submitted maintenance notification

3. F5777_TRAN | Maintenance Supervisor | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_PC

A user assigned with this AAV can work with notifications across all phases — from the moment a notification is raised to when it is completed. They can create, view, screen, accept, reject, and edit maintenance notifications. Editing is not phase-restricted; the supervisor can update a notification whether it is unscreened, in action-required state, or already accepted. The user can’t create or assign maintenance order for accepted notifications with this AAV.


Fig 6: Object page view for user with F5777_TRAN AAV when a notification is created

This AAV is part of the standard role template SAP_BR_MAINT_SUPERVISOR, belonging to business catalog SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_PC.

Unlike the AAV F5777_TRAN, the standard role template SAP_BR_MAINT_SUPERVISOR offers the user to even create or assign maintenance order for accepted notifications due to additional authorizations from other business catalogs in the role template.


Fig 7: Additional actions enabled in standard supervisor role template for accepted maintenance notification

4. F5777_EXCP_TRAN | SAP_EAM_BC_MN_MNG_PC

This variant gives a user maintenance employee-level access combined with an expanded emergency and minor work creation authorization for maintenance notifications — beyond what F5777_EMP_TRAN allows, but without the screening scope of F5777_TRAN.
This is the most nuanced of the four, and it exists for a very specific real-world situation – the Operator role.

The operator use case, addressed by F5777_EXCP_TRAN, is a good example of the kind of real-world role complexity that AAVs are designed to handle — cleanly, within the standard SAP authorization model.


Fig 8: Maintenance employee access extended with create minor and emergency work.

Note: The maintenance employee can be restricted to creating either emergency work or minor work along with standard maintenance notification by maintaining restrictions in the role assigned to the user. The restriction should be applied for 'Maintenance Notification Processing Context' to support either of the options-minor or emergency.


Fig 9: Restriction applied for Emergency Work (01)


Fig 10: User can only create emergency and standard maintenance notifications

This is a small example of how a single app can serve very different personas through AAVs — each variant reflecting a specific set of responsibilities without over- or under-provisioning access. 
You can see AAVs give you more precise control over authorizations, but as an admin, while designing roles, you should also consider what additional dependencies should be added to the role apart from the dependencies already proposed when adding an AAV.

entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Joule Response

Troubleshooting: Fiori Elements Object-Page Header & Navigation Hierarchy in RAP Composition

The slash-separated header values you are seeing (e.g., 8001 / on Customer Address and 8001 / / on Tax) are a classic symptom of Fiori Elements being unable to resolve the title or description annotation for one or more levels in the composition hierarchy. Fiori Elements for OData V2 builds the breadcrumb/header by traversing the composition chain upward and reading the @UI.headerInfo annotation at each level. When a level returns an empty or unresolved value, it renders as a blank segment — hence the trailing slashes.

Below is a structured diagnostic and resolution guide covering all three layers you asked about.

Possible Causes

  1. Missing or incorrect @UI.headerInfo annotations in one or more projection views — the most common root cause of blank slash segments.
  2. Parent association not correctly exposed or redirected in the projection view or projection behavior definition, preventing upward navigation context resolution.
  3. Composition or $self join condition mismatch across hierarchy levels, causing the framework to fail silently when resolving parent keys.
  4. OData V2 navigation property binding incomplete for nested entities beyond two levels deep, which is a known consideration for deeper composition trees. [1]

How Fiori Elements Resolves the Slash-Separated Header

In a RAP-based Fiori Elements OData V2 application, the object-page header breadcrumb is constructed as follows:

  • For each object page in the navigation stack, Fiori Elements reads the @UI.headerInfo.title.value (and optionally @UI.headerInfo.description.value) from the projection view of that entity.
  • It then traverses the parent association (association to parent) upward through the composition tree to obtain the parent's title for the breadcrumb prefix.
  • The slash separator is inserted between each resolved level.

If @UI.headerInfo.title.value points to a field that is null, empty, or not exposed in the projection view, that segment renders as blank — producing the 8001 / or 8001 / / pattern you observe. [2]

The depth of your hierarchy (Customer → Company Code → Tax = 3 levels) is supported by the framework — more than 3 levels are explicitly supported in RAP Fiori Elements. [1]

Resolution Steps

Step 1 — Verify @UI.headerInfo on Every Projection View

Check each projection view entity in your hierarchy. Every entity that has its own object page must declare:

 
@UI.headerInfo: {
  typeName: 'Customer Address',
  typeNamePlural: 'Customer Addresses',
  title: {
    type: #STANDARD,
    value: 'AddressID'          -- must be a non-null, exposed field
  },
  description: {
    type: #STANDARD,
    value: 'Street'             -- optional but recommended
  }
}

Critical checks:

  • The field referenced in title.value must be selected and exposed in the projection view — not just in the base/interface view.
  • For UUID-keyed entities, do not use the raw UUID as the title value unless you have a semantic label field. If no meaningful label exists, use a concatenated or virtual element.
  • For the Tax entity (child of Company Code, which is child of Customer), the header shows 8001 / / — meaning two levels above Tax are failing to resolve. Check both the Tax projection view and the Company Code projection view for missing @UI.headerInfo.title.value fields.
Step 2 — Check Parent Association Exposure in Projection Views

In each child projection view, the association to parent must be redirected to the corresponding consumption/projection view:

 
-- In the Customer Address projection view (ZC_CustomerAddress):
define view entity ZC_CustomerAddress
  as projection on ZI_CustomerAddress
{
  key CustomerAddressUUID,
  CustomerUUID,
  Street,
  City,
  -- ...
  /* Associations */
  _Customer : redirected to parent ZC_Customer   -- MUST be present
}

If _Customer is not redirected to the projection-layer parent (ZC_Customer), Fiori Elements cannot traverse upward to resolve the parent's title for the breadcrumb. [3] [4] [5]

For the Tax entity (two levels deep under Customer), the chain must be complete:

  • Tax projection → _CompanyCode : redirected to parent ZC_CompanyCode
  • Company Code projection → _Customer : redirected to parent ZC_Customer

A break at any level in this chain causes blank segments in the header.

Step 3 — Validate Composition and Association Definitions in Behavior Definitions

In the projection behavior definition, verify that the parent association is exposed for each child entity:

 
projection;

define behavior for ZC_Customer alias Customer
{
  use create;
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _CustomerRole { create; }
  use association _CustomerAddress { create; }
  use association _CompanyCode { create; }
}

define behavior for ZC_CustomerAddress alias CustomerAddress
{
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _Customer;   -- parent association must be declared here
}

define behavior for ZC_CompanyCode alias CompanyCode
{
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _Customer;   -- parent association
  use association _Tax { create; }
}

define behavior for ZC_Tax alias Tax
{
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _CompanyCode;  -- parent association
}

If the parent association is not declared with use association in the projection behavior definition, the OData V2 service will not generate the corresponding navigation property, and Fiori Elements cannot resolve the upward navigation context. [3] [4]

Step 4 — Inspect the OData V2 Service Binding

After correcting annotations and behavior definitions, re-activate the service binding and verify in the service preview:

  • Each entity set must have navigation properties pointing to its parent entity set.
  • For Tax (two levels deep), you should see navigation properties: _CompanyCode on the Tax entity set, and _Customer on the Company Code entity set.
  • If navigation properties are missing, the root cause is typically the missing use association _Parent in the projection behavior definition (Step 3).

For OData V2 specifically, navigation property resolution for nested entities beyond two levels requires that every intermediate association is correctly exposed — there is no automatic inference across skipped levels. [6] [7]

Key Annotation & Definition Checks

Layer What to Check Expected Behavior
CDS Projection View@UI.headerInfo.title.value on every entity with an object pageDisplays a meaningful, non-null label per entity in the breadcrumb
CDS Projection View_Parent : redirected to parent ZC_<ParentEntity>Enables upward navigation context resolution
Projection Behavior Definitionuse association _Parent; declared for each child entityOData V2 generates the navigation property for parent traversal
Interface (Base) Viewassociation to parent ZI_<ParentEntity> as _Parent on $projection.<ParentUUID> = _Parent.<ParentUUID>Correct join condition — UUID field names must match exactly
Service DefinitionAll entities (Customer, CustomerRole, CustomerAddress, CompanyCode, Tax) explicitly listedAll entity sets and navigation properties are generated in the OData metadata
OData V2 BindingNavigation properties visible in service preview for each child→parent directionHeader resolves parent key and title correctly at each level

Summary of the Most Likely Root Cause for Your Specific Pattern

Observed Header Most Likely Missing Element
8001 / on Customer Address@UI.headerInfo.title.value on the Customer Address projection view is missing or points to a null/unexposed field
8001 / / on Tax@UI.headerInfo.title.value missing on both Company Code and Tax projection views, or the parent association chain is broken at the Company Code → Customer level

Start by auditing the @UI.headerInfo annotation on the Company Code and Tax projection views first, then verify the _Parent association redirect and use association _Parent in the projection behavior definition for those two entities. [2]

entry.title: SAP Table to CDS Mapper - New Version thanks to AI-supported Development
entry.content:
TL;DR

I created a standalone HTML analysis that helps developers find possible CDS objects from a standard SAP table or table field. It combines direct field lineage with official successor hints and Cloudification Repository C1-release evidence. The snapshot covers 121,303 successfully analyzed CDS objects, 20,028 physical tables, and 1,647,510 direct field mappings and showed promising successors for over 2,000 tables that have no official successor at the moment.

Download the analysis package (ZIP). Extract it and open the HTML file; no SAP-system installation or additional service is required.
**This is a discovery accelerator, not an SAP replacement decision. The developer must validate business scope, semantics, authorizations, and performance for the intended use case.**

What is the issue here?

Finding a possible CDS object for a familiar SAP table is still more difficult than it should be. The Cloudification Repository, released object trees in ADT, and the SAP Business Accelerator Hub are valuable starting points. But successor information is not available for every table, and developers often start with a table and a field rather than the business-object vocabulary needed to find the right CDS object.

In my earlier post, How to find a CDS view for a classic Table in ABAP - Cheat Sheet, I described a pragmatic way to reverse-engineer direct table-to-CDS field relationships. This post takes the same idea one step further: I ran the analysis broadly on an SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01 system and created a portable report that lets a developer start from a standard table or a table field.

Important disclaimer: This is not an SAP tool and it is not a replacement-decision engine. It is an accelerator for discovering candidate CDS objects. A structural field mapping, a C1-release indicator, or even an official-successor indication does not prove semantic, functional, authorization, cardinality, filtering, or performance equivalence. The developer still has to validate that a candidate fits the concrete requirement.

Why an additional mapping is useful

The usual SAP tools rely heavily on maintained successor information. That is the strongest signal where it exists. However, not every classic table has a maintained successor. And an object can map relevant fields without being listed as a formal successor.

One useful example is T001L, the storage-location table. In the analyzed snapshot, it has no official-successor entry. Nevertheless, the report identifies I_StorageLocation as a C1-released candidate with direct mappings for 9 of the 22 persisted table fields. This is not a statement that I_StorageLocation replaces every T001L use case. It is a concrete, inspectable starting point for a developer who otherwise might not know where to look.

Using a deliberately cautious rule (no explicit official successor, a C1-release signal, at least three directly mapped fields, at least 30% direct coverage, excluding CUBE and value help views) the snapshot identifies 2,071 DB tables with a C1 released view as starting point. The Table explorer marks these as Good C1 candidate available and can filter for them. This is a prioritization signal only: it does not make the candidate an official successor or guarantee that it is suitable for a specific requirement.

For teams using Project Kernseife, I also provide a BF5 External classification import for these 2,071 additional successors. Choose not to overwrite existing classifications if you want to leave any existing custom classification untouched; those existing records will not be replaced by this import. If you choose overwrite instead, review the complete classification and preserve any existing successors that must remain. The classification is still only a curated discovery aid: validate that each CDS candidate fits the required business scope and works for the intended use case before relying on it.

What was analyzed

The snapshot was compiled in October 2026 on SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01. It contains metadata only; no business data was read or exported.

  • 130,647 CDS entities were placed in the extraction queue.
  • 121,303 CDS entities were analyzed successfully.
  • 20,028 physical base tables have persisted field-denominator metadata in the local report.
  • 1,647,510 non-calculated direct field-mapping rows are available for analysis.

* Not every available CDS object could be analyzed. This does not remove the value of the evidence that is present, but it means the report must not be interpreted as a complete catalog or a replacement decision.

How the data is compiled

The technical core is SAP class CL_DD_DDL_FIELD_TRACKER. For each analyzed CDS definition, it provides base-field information. The extractor keeps direct relationships between a CDS element and an underlying table field. Calculated elements are retained separately where useful, but they do not increase direct field coverage.

The process is broadly:

  1. Discover relevant standard CDS definitions in the analyzed system.
  2. Read direct CDS-element-to-base-table-field lineage.
  3. Persist physical-table field metadata so coverage can be calculated.
  4. Enrich CDS candidates with effective release, C1/cloud-usage, and official-successor evidence when the system provides it.
  5. Reverse the result: table and table field to candidate CDS entities and elements.
  6. Rank candidates: official successor first, then C1-released candidates, then direct field coverage.

I am especially grateful to Andreas Graeber. He shared the idea and solution with me before he open sourced and published CDS Analyser. Publishing it gave the community a practical implementation to inspect, reuse, and improve. This analysis builds on that generous contribution.

As mentioned in the title - this was done leveraging a new AI harness, so I tried "Hermes" for the first time (and quite liked it). I admit, it is mainly vibe-coded, so if you have ideas on how to improve this, feel free to take it from here!

How to use the report

The report has three views:

  • Use and limitations explains the purpose, evidence model, and validation boundary.
  • Table explorer lets a developer search a table, inspect the ranked candidate CDS objects, filter for official successors, C1-released candidates, or the cautious good-candidate signal, and expand a candidate to see the direct field mappings.
  • Overview provides aggregate coverage and concentration statistics for the snapshot.

You can identify possible successors in the Table explorer as shown in this example for T001L, which indicates I_StorageLocation as C1-released view that is worth diving into:

 

The field filter is especially useful for focused questions. For example, a developer can select EKKO, enter STCEG, and see only CDS candidates with a direct mapping for that field. The same filter updates field coverage. Candidate filters also update coverage: if the developer selects only C1-released candidates, fields that are not mapped by any C1 candidate are shown as gaps.

Evidence, not a guarantee

This distinction matters. A CDS object can deliberately model only part of a table's scope. The well-known repository-directory example of TADIR is useful here: a CDS object like the successor I_CUSTABAPOBJDIRECTORYENTRY may expose customer-created repository objects while intentionally excluding standard objects. A high mapping percentage can therefore still be wrong for a particular consumer.

For that reason, the report makes the evidence visible instead of turning it into a binary recommendation:

  • Official successor means that the system provides explicit successor evidence.
  • C1 released means that the snapshot found C1-release evidence for ABAP Cloud usage.
  • Coverage means direct structural field mapping, not business equivalence.
  • Good C1 candidate available is a cautious discovery filter for tables without official successor evidence; it is neither an SAP endorsement nor a replacement guarantee.
  • Unreleased candidates remain visible for investigation but are not presented as released API recommendations.

This aligns with the broader Clean Core principle: release information is important guidance, but developers still need to understand the intended API and validate that it meets their use case. The mapping helps to reduce the time spent searching; it does not remove engineering judgment.

Where this can help next

I see this primarily as a discovery aid for modernization work, custom-code remediation, and development teams that are moving away from direct table access. It can also support project-specific governance: once a team has validated suitable CDS objects for its relevant scenarios, those decisions can be maintained as explicit project rules rather than rediscovered repeatedly.

The result is provided as a standalone HTML analysis. Like the Excel sheet in the earlier post, it can be opened and used directly without installing anything in an SAP system or running an additional service. Refreshing the analysis for a later Feature Package Stack is still necessary, because available CDS content and release status can change.

If you use this kind of mapping, I would be interested in hearing which evidence you find most useful: official successors, C1 release, direct coverage, field-level lookup, or additional factors such as key fields and business-object metadata.

References

  • How to find a CDS view for a classic Table in ABAP - Cheat Sheet
  • agraeber/cdsanalyser
  • Cloudification Repository Viewer
  • Project Kernseife
